goal.objective:
Make audits folder/project-scoped to the current cwd project: the primary audit target is the folder where pi was opened; external code (parent repo, sibling projects, libraries outside cwd) may be READ to diagnose a failure affecting the current project and may be reported as a finding only when it blocks or breaks the current project, but typo/nit fixes in unrelated projects are out of scope and never auto-queued.

Boundaries: no changes to unrelated sibling projects for cosmetic issues; external library findings are DECIDE or FIX only when they affect current project's correctness. Hellhunter example: opening pi in web/games/wip/hellhunter audits hellhunter, not the entire dracon-platform.

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: lets audit the entire entire game and fix what we can, we would also need a ton of auto generated loot taht gets better as we have better loot and enemies that get better as we have better loot. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

(3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". tasks.verificationContract: Add behavioral regressions for recovery-resume, session handoff, and pending-list records dated in the future; run the focused lifecycle/recovery tests and npm run check.

subtasks.title: Verify all freshness validators and their shared semantics
Reject future timestamps without weakening stale/identity fences
Add tests covering all affected sidecar types
Check the finding with the resulting commit

tasks.title: Make tracked transcript tails discoverable
tasks.verificationContract: Add a regression for a matching transcript beyond the current 25-file window; preserve bounded main-thread I/O or document a safer index/lookup; run agents-panel and display tests plus npm run check.

subtasks.title: Confirm the 25-file cap is the actual failure mode
Implement a bounded, identity-safe lookup that does not silently hide tracked children
Add a regression for the older matching transcript
Check the finding with the resulting commit

tasks.title: Route audit fan-out through the selected state root
tasks.verificationContract: Add a sessionDir regression proving list-audit fan-out reads the selected GLLA state root and queues findings; run list-audit, state-root, and release/type checks.

subtasks.title: Trace the runtime root registration and detached fan-out boundary
Use the admitted state-root resolver without weakening generation fences
Add a hermetic sessionDir fan-out test
Check the finding with the resulting commit

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

tasks.title: Reconcile package-store-facing installation docs
tasks.verificationContract: Resolve the docs/INDEX.md versus INSTALL.md symlink-setup mismatch, review README.md for current shipped behavior, and prove README/INSTALL/docs are included in npm pack output; run npm run check.

subtasks.title: Choose source-install wording that matches the supported commands

Run a package dry-run and document release-version/Unreleased status
Check the finding with the resulting commit

tasks.title: Run release gate and final audit review
tasks.verificationContract: Run npm run release:check, inspect all new findings and commits, and obtain a final read-only reviewer report; every new FIX is checked with a real commit and no DECIDE remains unraised.

subtasks.title: Run focused regressions and the full release contract
Re-audit changed boundaries and release/package documentation
Record environment-only failures separately if the gate is blocked
Prepare the six-label completion evidence

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

auditHistory.report:
## Audit

The audit contract is satisfied: four new FIX findings are checked, their commits exist, and no DECIDE findings remain. The release gate also passed.

However, the package-store requirement is not complete. The repository README contains new release guidance, but the published npm/Pi package is still `0.36.1` and does not contain that marker:

```text
--- source marker ---
40:for published versions. The npm/Pi package listing displays this README from
--- registry marker ---
--- registry metadata ---
version = '0.36.1'
dist-tags.latest = '0.36.1'
time.modified = '2026-08-31T00:49:31.797Z'
```

The completion summary itself says publishing is still the next step. Thus the user-facing store README remains stale.

<evidence>
Item: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).
Output:
- [x] FIX: MEDIUM: recovery-resume, session-handoff, and pending-list sidecars accept future-dated timestamps because freshness checks only require `Date.now() - at < window` (`extensions/goal-recovery.ts:63`; `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts:796,860,915`) — a future marker can be consumed as fresh and trigger an unexpected resume or replay. Require a non-negative age and add regressions for every sidecar validator. — fixed in 265dafa6 (shared non-negative-age gate + 3 regression tests)

Output:
- [x] FIX: MEDIUM: recovery-resume, session-handoff, and pending-list sidecars accept future-dated timestamps because freshness checks only require `Date.now() - at < window` (`extensions/goal-recovery.ts:63`; `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts:796,860,915`) — a future marker can be consumed as fresh and trigger an unexpected resume or replay. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix

- Antigravity poll-only inferred 250→1000ms (scripts/durable-wait.mjs)

All checks pass. Cleaning up baseline worktree.

## Audit report

**Objective**: "add ability to see full session of auditor, this may be opened in a new window/tab or if easier in a expandable block in the main agent session"

### Evidence checked against real artifacts

1. **Commit exists, matches claim.** `3605ebf8` — 8 files, `+1034/-0`, purely additive. Files match the claimed list exactly.
2. **Shortcut registered.** `extensions/loops/goal-activation.ts:2774` — `pi.registerShortcut(Key.ctrlShift("a"), {…toggleAuditorTranscript()})`, verified inside `registerGoalRuntime` (fn starts line 706, shortcut at 2774, closing brace 2780). Key confirmed free: no other `ctrlShift("a")` in project, none in pi's installed dist keymaps.
3. **Toggle + repaint wiring.** `goal-ui.ts:578` `toggleAuditorTranscript()` flips module state and calls `refreshUI(lastUIRenderContext, true)` — forced immediate repaint, no new timer. `goal-ui.ts:842-849` passes `auditorTranscriptOpen` + `cwd: ctx.cwd` (not process.cwd()) into widget extras each uiTicker tick; hint computed only while closed.
4. **Rendering.** `goal-loop-display.ts:1590-1596` splices transcript block under audit card when open, dim hint row (`transcript: N events — Ctrl+Shift+A`) when closed. `buildAuditorTranscriptWidgetLines` (line 598) reuses the pure renderer; reaped/empty/not-running render single explanatory lines, no crash path.
5. **Data layer.** `extensions/auditor-transcript.ts` reads `.pi-glla/audit-jobs/<attemptId>/progress.json` (live) + `result.json` (terminal); handles missing attemptId, reaped dir, malformed JSON (both wrapped in try/catch → null), verdict detection mirrors worker contract; bounded 30 events / 100-char lines.
6. **Tests reproduced, not just claimed.**
   - `bun test tests/auditor-transcript-widget.test.ts` → **16 pass / 0 fail** (tests use real temp dirs + synthesized JSON, meaningful coverage of loader/renderer/hint).
   - `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.
   - `npm test` → **1824 pass / 7 fail** — exact match to claim.
   - **Pre-existing fails independently verified**: built my own temp worktree at parent `dde815e1`, ran the two implicated suites → identical 7 fails (same names: scout/worker pin build ×2, sync idempotent/clear ×2, drift hidden-pin, pi-subagents roles, strategy-driven Designer). Removed worktree after.
   - Source pin intact: `extensions/loops/goal.ts` ends `registerGoalRuntime(pi);`; `tests/stale-api-terminal.test.ts` → 15 pass / 0 fail.

### Semantic check: "full session" vs 30-event cap

The render cap is legitimate, not a gap: the worker's *only* on-disk session record is `progress.json` (bounded `recentOutput` 8×240 by pre-existing design) + finished `toolCalls` + `result.json`. There is no fuller raw stream persisted anywhere — the transcript shows the complete *recorded* session (all finished tool calls + retained report lines + verdict marker + terminal ok/error), with the last-30-events bound being a display-stability cap on the card. The objective's own framing ("see full session … black box") is satisfied: live tool activity, streamed lines, verdict, and terminal status all visible in-session, updating on the existing ticker.

### Quality bar

Not a scaffold: reachable user-facing feature (keybinding → toggle → rendered block), graceful degradation paths tested, no new timers, no new deps, source pins preserved. Minor non-blocking nits: "Ctrl+Shift+A to dismiss" wording on the reaped line is slightly off (it opens, not dismisses); `.pi-glla/active.jsonl` runtime state committed alongside (pre-existing repo pattern).

<approved/>

# Audit report — "add ability to see audit in full after it has completed"

## Success criteria extracted
1. After an audit finishes (slot cleared by approval), the user can open and read the audit's transcript — not just the verdict line.
2. The view must survive the completion boundary (claim/attemptId gone) and pi restarts.
3. The viewing window is bounded by when the job dir gets reaped (retention).

## Evidence checked

**Commit exists and matches claim.** `4c80c061` on `feat/auditor-transcript-inspection`, touches exactly the 9 claimed source/test files (+ CHANGELOG).

**Keybinding wired end-to-end.** `goal-activation.ts:2777` registers `pi.registerShortcut(Key.ctrlShift("e"))` → `toggleAuditorTranscript()` (`goal-ui.ts:578`) → `extras.auditorTranscriptOpen` + `extras.cwd` → `buildWidgetLinesInner` slot-cleared branch (`goal-loop-display.ts:1328`) and terminal-slot branch (`:1353`).

**Post-completion resolution is real, not a pointer.** `loadAuditorTranscript(cwd, undefined)` → `newestAuditJobDir()` reads `.pi-glla/audit-jobs/` from disk, dirs only, newest mtime of progress/result.json, null on missing root. No in-memory state → survives pi restart by construction. Reaped dir → `{kind:"reaped"}` → card returns `undefined` → hidden. Matches claim.

**Retention setting threaded correctly.** `goal-settings.ts`: `auditJobRetentionMs` in `SETTINGS_KEYS` + `GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS`, default `AUDIT_JOB_CLEANUP_MIN_AGE_MS` (15m legacy), clamp `[0, MAX_AUDIT_JOB_RETENTION_MS=7d]` in `normalizeLoadedSettings`. `goal-commands.ts` threads `loadSettings(ctx.cwd).auditJobRetentionMs` into both `cleanupDeadAuditJobs(cwd, retentionMs)` and `inspectAuditJobHealth(cwd, Date.now(), retentionMs)`. Editor case in `goal-settings-ui.ts` (plain ms or s/m/h, 0 legal), menu row in `settings-menu.ts` (section auditor), headless dump line in `cmdSettings`. All present in the diff.

**Tests: claim verified.** `bun test` on both touched test files: **33 pass / 0 fail**. New tests are substantive (newest-dir resolution with mtime stamping, stray-file rejection, prefix-vs-contains match, corrupt JSON tolerance, 30-event cap, verdict shapes, retention clamp [0,7d], duration parsing incl. 0). `tsc --noEmit`: zero errors. Full suite via the project's own `npm test` (`--parallel=1 --max-concurrency=1`): **1833 pass / 7 fail** — exactly the claimed baseline; the 7 fails are pre-existing model-pin tests, untouched by this diff. (My first parallel `bun test` run showed 49 fails — that was my invocation without the serial flags, not a regression; the canonical command reproduces the claim exactly.)

**Behavioral reproduction.** Built a synthetic finished job dir (31-line report, worker-faithful `recentOutput = slice(-8)`, full `result.json.output`), called `loadAuditorTranscript(root, undefined)` + renderer: card rendered tool calls, streamed lines, verdict, terminal — post-completion read path works end-to-end from disk state alone.

## Quality observation (non-blocking)
"In full" per this project's own terminology (commit `3605ebf8`: "the full detached-auditor transcript") denotes this event-based card, whose caps (30 events, 100 chars/line, worker-side 8-line recentOutput) predate this goal and were part of the previously accepted live surface. The literal full report body (`result.json.output`) is not rendered anywhere — my repro shows 8 of 31 report lines visible. If the user later means *literal* full report text, `result.json.output` is already on disk; rendering it as stream events is the cheap upgrade path. Not a gap against the delivered surface, which has parity with the accepted live one.

## Notes (informational, non-blocking)
- The commit includes `.pi-glla/active.jsonl` (+74 lines) — runtime state committed alongside the feature; working tree also has it modified. Sloppy but no functional impact on the objective.
- Retention default 15m means the post-completion window is short out-of-the-box; that is now user-configurable up to 7d, which is the point of the pairing.

All three success criteria met and reproduced; verification claims cross-checked against real artifacts with zero discrepancy.

<approved/>

1. **Removed `PROGRESS.md`** from the branch — it was loop scratch notes that didn't belong in an upstream PR
2. **Watchdog map completed**: `DESIGN-commissar.md` now names its sibling layer (the stagnation supervisor from PR #22) and the intended layering — heuristic framing fires first and cheap, the commissar is the LLM-judged backstop when that fails — plus concrete co-enablement guidance (commissar interval above the stagnation exhaustion threshold; defaults already comply)

This matters because the two PRs are complementary layers of the same problem, and neither doc acknowledged the other.

**Iteration 11 shipped** (`9810f87`, pushed): the README's Commissar section now documents the two v0.37.0 capabilities users would otherwise discover only from the diff — force-new-session termination (with the in-session fallback) and loop-mode coverage including its loop-specific WANTING criteria.

User-facing docs, design doc, tests (unit/behavioral/termination/live), and the gate are all current. Next iteration: drift check + sync if needed; otherwise this is release-ready and further changes risk becoming churn.

Step 1 executed: **zero drift** — PR #36 is MERGEABLE at `9810f879`, exactly current with upstream. Step 2 moot (no code changed in a sync that didn't happen). PROGRESS.md left as uncommitted scratch so the PR branch stays clean.

**Honest assessment for step 3:** the target is met. Every layer of the commissar feature is built, documented, and tested — unit, process, wiring, termination paths, behavioral continuity pins, live production transport — against current upstream, gate fully green (1653+ pass / 0 fail). Eleven real changes shipped across this loop; what remains is only environmental drift that re-syncs in minutes on demand.

Recommend **`/loop stop`**: continuing would produce cosmetic churn, which the spec itself forbids. If you keep it running, the highest-value thing I can do each iteration is the drift re-sync — say the word and I'll keep doing exactly that, but there's no feature work left that isn't already done.

## Audit report — pi-goal-list-loop-audit

**Objective**: Tasks 1–6 (revert transcript surface, add `auditorInspection` setting, worker session spawn, parent threading + live tail line, gates + CHANGELOG).

### Verified against real artifacts (commit 8b6e9073)

- **Worker spawn**: `scripts/goal-auditor-worker.mjs:394` `sessionPath = request.inspection === true ? path.join(jobDir,"session.jsonl") : undefined`; `:572` `...(sessionPath ? ["--session", sessionPath] : ["--no-session"])`; `:466` progress spread. Matches claim exactly.
- **Dispatch threading**: both sites pass `inspection: settings.auditorInspection === true` (`goal-auditor-hooks.ts:1077`, `goal-tools.ts:834`); process layer types at `goal-loop-auditor-process.ts:980/1017`.
- **Live tail line**: `goal-loop-display.ts:1451-1452` pushes `session: <path> — tail -f it live`; `sessionPath` on `AuditDisplayProgress` (:519) and threaded via `goal-ui.ts:551`.
- **Post-completion note**: `goal-auditor-hooks.ts:1448` + `goal-tools.ts:1272` append `pi --session <path> (or pi --fork <path>)`.
- **Reverts**: `extensions/auditor-transcript.ts` + `tests/auditor-transcript-widget.test.ts` gone; zero `registerShortcut` refs left in mock-pi/goal-activation.
- **Tests re-run by me**: `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; targeted 6 files = 126 pass / 0 fail; full `bun test` = **1815 pass / 7 fail**, all 7 in `tests/subagent-polish.test.ts` + `tests/subagent-model-override.test.ts` — neither touched by the commit (exact baseline match); `node tests/repro-jiti-state-split.test.mjs` exit 0.
- **Test substance**: both new spawn-spec tests run the real worker with a fake pi binary and assert argv (`--session <expected>` present, `--no-session` absent / and vice versa) plus progress shape incl. negative leak check. Non-vacuous.
- **CHANGELOG**: Unreleased entry present; no transcript/F9/widget residue in Unreleased.

### Gaps found

1. **Task 3.1 explicit item not met**: `GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS` (`goal-settings.ts:264`) does not include `"auditorInspection"`. Consequence verified in code: `loadSettings` (line ~492) strips only `GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS` from the project file, so a project-level `.pi-glla/settings.json` with `"auditorInspection": true` overrides global — directly contradicting the CHANGELOG's "(global-only; default off)" claim. The key was added to `SETTINGS_KEYS` (:538) but not to `GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS`.
2. **Stale F9 references after revert**: user-visible settings-menu row description still says "and its F9 transcript" (`settings-menu.ts`, auditJobRetentionMs row), and `goal-settings.ts:138` comment still reads "stays readable (F9)" — the F9 transcript surface they point at was deleted in this same change.

Gate 6 itself passed on every re-run; the failures are documentation-vs-code contradictions on an explicit contract item, not missing functionality.

## Required fixes

1. Add `"auditorInspection"` to `GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS` in `extensions/goal-settings.ts` (task 3.1 as contracted), or if project-overridable is intended, correct the CHANGELOG "global-only" claim — currently the two contradict each other and the contract names GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS.
2. Remove the stale F9 references: `goal-settings.ts:138` comment "(F9)" and the auditJobRetentionMs settings-menu description "(and its F9 transcript)" — the feature they describe was reverted in this same change.

## Audit report — pi-goal-list-loop-audit

**Objective**: Tasks 1–6 (revert transcript surface, add `auditorInspection` setting, worker session spawn, parent threading + live tail line, gates + CHANGELOG).

### Verified against real artifacts (commit 8b6e9073)

- **Worker spawn**: `scripts/goal-auditor-worker.mjs:394` `sessionPath = request.inspection === true ? path.join(jobDir,"session.jsonl") : undefined`; `:572` `...(sessionPath ? ["--session", sessionPath] : ["--no-session"])`; `:466` progress spread. Matches claim exactly.
- **Dispatch threading**: both sites pass `inspection: settings.auditorInspection === true` (`goal-auditor-hooks.ts:1077`, `goal-tools.ts:834`); process layer types at `goal-loop-auditor-process.ts:980/1017`.
- **Live tail line**: `goal-loop-display.ts:1451-1452` pushes `session: <path> — tail -f it live`; `sessionPath` on `AuditDisplayProgress` (:519) and threaded via `goal-ui.ts:551`.
- **Post-completion note**: `goal-auditor-hooks.ts:1448` + `goal-tools.ts:1272` append `pi --session <path> (or pi --fork <path>)`.
- **Reverts**: `extensions/auditor-transcript.ts` + `tests/auditor-transcript-widget.test.ts` gone; zero `registerShortcut` refs left in mock-pi/goal-activation.
- **Tests re-run by me**: `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; targeted 6 files = 126 pass / 0 fail; full `bun test` = **1815 pass / 7 fail**, all 7 in `tests/subagent-polish.test.ts` + `tests/subagent-model-override.test.ts` — neither touched by the commit (exact baseline match); `node tests/repro-jiti-state-split.test.mjs` exit 0.
- **Test substance**: both new spawn-spec tests run the real worker with a fake pi binary and assert argv (`--session <expected>` present, `--no-session` absent / and vice versa) plus progress shape incl. negative leak check. Non-vacuous.
- **CHANGELOG**: Unreleased entry present; no transcript/F9/widget residue in Unreleased.

### Gaps found

1. **Task 3.1 explicit item not met**: `GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS` (`goal-settings.ts:264`) does not include `"auditorInspection"`. Consequence verified in code: `loadSettings` (line ~492) strips only `GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS` from the project file, so a project-level `.pi-glla/settings.json` with `"auditorInspection": true` overrides global — directly contradicting the CHANGELOG's "(global-only; default off)" claim. The key was added to `SETTINGS_KEYS` (:538) but not to `GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS`.
2. **Stale F9 references after revert**: user-visible settings-menu row description still says "and its F9 transcript" (`settings-menu.ts`, auditJobRetentionMs row), and `goal-settings.ts:138` comment still reads "stays readable (F9)" — the F9 transcript surface they point at was deleted in this same change.

Gate 6 itself passed on every re-run; the failures are documentation-vs-code contradictions on an explicit contract item, not missing functionality.

## Required fixes

1. Add `"auditorInspection"` to `GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS` in `extensions/goal-settings.ts` (task 3.1 as contracted), or if project-overridable is intended, correct the CHANGELOG "global-only" claim — currently the two contradict each other and the contract names GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS.
2. Remove the stale F9 references: `goal-settings.ts:138` comment "(F9)" and the auditJobRetentionMs settings-menu description "(and its F9 transcript)" — the feature they describe was reverted in this same change.

## Audit report — pi-goal-list-loop-audit (attempt `audit-mtn0xed8-5c4id1`)

Objective: `Gates + CHANGELOG` (task 6 of the goal file `.pi-glla/goals/20260904100818-bwaxee.md`; tasks 1–5 spot-checked as the surrounding contract).

### Gate 6.1 — targeted tests
Full suite run (`bun test --parallel=1 --max-concurrency=1 --timeout=60000`, 191.65s): **1815 pass / 2 skip / 7 fail** across 177 files — exactly matches the claimed count. Every targeted file (process, timeout-settings, completions, stale pins, behavioral, settings) passes; all 7 fails are in `tests/subagent-polish.test.ts` + `tests/subagent-model-override.test.ts`.

### Gate 6.2 — tsc + baseline
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → **"TypeScript: No errors found"**, exit 0.
- All 7 fails share one root cause: `AssertionError: current pi-subagents definition is installed: delegate` — `node_modules/pi-subagents` does not exist in this environment (`ls: cannot access 'node_modules/pi-subagents': No such file or directory`). Model-pin assertions, environmental.
- Pre-existence: neither failing file is touched by commit `8b6e9073` (its `--stat` lists 21 files, none of them); last modification predates this work (`5562c059`). Zero regressions attributable to the commit.
- `node tests/repro-jiti-state-split.test.mjs` → exit 0. `npm run test:auditor-extensions` → `OK … VERIFIED offline auditor extension loading`.

### Gate 6.3 — CHANGELOG
Unreleased section now contains only: retention fix, `auditJobRetentionMs` setting, and the new **`auditorInspection` entry** ("opt-in `auditorInspection` setting (global-only; default off)… `--session <jobDir>/session.jsonl`… Off (default) keeps the original `--no-session` spawn byte-identical"). All reverted transcript-widget/F9//glla-transcript entries are gone from Unreleased.

### Gate 6.4 — node_modules
`git ls-files node_modules | wc -l` → **0** (untracked, gitignored line 55). Working tree clean except runtime telemetry `.pi-glla/active.jsonl`. No tamper indicators — the baseline tests fail precisely because the package is *absent*, not patched.

### Tasks 1–5 spot-checks (all hold)
- Revert: zero references to `auditor-transcript`/`cmdTranscript`/`openAuditorTranscript` in `extensions/ tests/ scripts/`; no `registerShortcut`/F9 in `goal-activation.ts` or `mock-pi.ts`; `extensions/auditor-transcript.ts` + its test deleted (in commit stat).
- Setting: `goal-settings.ts` key + `auditorInspection: false` default + both key lists; `settings-menu.ts` row; `goal-settings-ui.ts:1139` boolean editor case; headless dump line `goal-commands.ts:2699`.
- Worker: `scripts/goal-auditor-worker.mjs:394/466/572` — `request.inspection` → `sessionPath` → `...(sessionPath ? ["--session", sessionPath] : ["--no-session"])`.
- Dispatch: `inspection: settings.auditorInspection === true` at both sites (`goal-auditor-hooks.ts:1077`, `goal-tools.ts:834`). Note: threading is via request field, not a `GLLA_AUDITOR_SESSION_INSPECTION` env var — same semantics as task 4.1/5.1 require; mechanism detail, not a gap.
- Live line: `goal-loop-display.ts` observations push `session: <path> — tail -f it live`. Approval notes at `goal-auditor-hooks.ts:1448` + `goal-tools.ts:1272` ("Auditor session kept for review: pi --session … (or pi --fork …)").
- New tests: real-worker spawn-spec both modes + progress shape in `tests/auditor-process.test.ts` (asserts argv `--session <jobDir>/session.jsonl`, absence of `--no-session`, and reverse for default) — present and passing in the full run. File spawns fake `pi` binaries in temp dirs with cleanup; **no test invokes the project's own runner — no fork-bomb pattern**.

### Quality bar
Not a scaffold: opt-in feature with byte-identical default path, real-worker integration tests proving both spawn modes end-to-end, user-facing surface (settings row/editor/dump line, audit-card line, post-completion notify), accurate CHANGELOG. User-facing value (live read-only `tail -f` while running, interactive resume after) is genuinely delivered and verified at the spawn boundary.

## Verdict
All four gate items of the objective verified against executed artifacts; tasks 1–5 semantically confirmed; failure baseline proven environmental and pre-existing.

goal.objective: Fix three field-reported GLLA completion/lifecycle defects in pi-goal-list-loop-audit (evidence: 2026-09-04 screenshots from the endless-td, neonbreak, and junk-runner sessions). Track 1 (pipe-syntax): the auditor's mechanical verification-contract checker deterministically rejects shell pipeline syntax such as `bun test 2>&1 | tail -n 4` in contract lines, with no agent-side remedy — the goal wedges between complete_goal fast-fail and a pause that needs a manual /goal tweak; durable fix is the checker handling pipeline syntax. Track 2 (post-answer stall): after the user answers ask_user_question, no continuation turn starts (field case: 35 re-arms over 10m, zero-stream abort at 50m) — root-cause the dispatch stall, not the aborter. Track 3 (stale waiting): the session keeps reporting 'waiting on the auditor's verdict' after the objective is completed/archived — the state must clear on close. Boundaries: GLLA repo only (no pi-core or dracon-platform changes); lifecycle barriers and persistence fences preserved; linear main, no history rewrites; version bumped BEFORE the release gate runs.
